text:
acme-devops: Hey, after we locked down egress with a default-deny NP our redwood-agent (namespace: redwood-private) can't register. Logs show timeouts and TLS failures. Opening thread.

sarah: Sorry — can you paste agent logs + the NetworkPolicy and try DNS/curl from the pod?

acme-devops: Logs:
```
[2026-04-02T14:03:11Z] INFO starting redwood-agent v2.2.0
[2026-04-02T14:03:13Z] WARN register: dial tcp 54.210.99.12:443: i/o timeout
[2026-04-02T14:03:13Z] ERROR tls: handshake failed: remote error: tls: protocol version not supported
```
NetworkPolicy we applied (redwood-egress-restrict):
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: redwood-egress-restrict
  namespace: redwood-private
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redwood-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          env: infra
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

mike: That NP only allows to pods labelled env=infra in-cluster. That won't let the agent talk to external control-plane IPs or DNS. Run these inside the agent pod and paste output:
```
kubectl exec -n redwood-private <pod> -- dig +short control.redwood.example.com @10.96.0.10 || true
kubectl exec -n redwood-private <pod> -- curl -v --connect-timeout 5 https://control.redwood.example.com:443/health || true
kubectl exec -n redwood-private <pod> -- ip route; ip addr show; cat /etc/resolv.conf || true
kubectl exec -n redwood-private <pod> -- tcpdump -n -c 10 -i eth0 port 53 or port 443 || true
```

acme-devops: Results:
```
$ dig +short control.redwood.example.com @10.96.0.10
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached

$ curl -v https://control.redwood.example.com:443/health
*   Trying 54.210.99.12:443...
* connect to 54.210.99.12 port 443 failed: Connection timed out

$ cat /etc/resolv.conf
nameserver 10.96.0.10

$ tcpdump output (abbrev):
09:15:12 IP 10.244.0.23.54321 > 54.210.99.12.443: SYN
09:15:12 IP 10.244.0.23.54322 > 10.96.0.10.53: UDP
# no SYN-ACKs returned
```

dan: Two things jumping out: DNS to cluster DNS is blocked (no UDP/53), and SYNs to external IPs go out with pod source IP (10.244.0.23). If your infra firewall only allows NATed node IPs, the firewall will drop pod IP traffic. Do you have node SNAT/MASQ configured? On many clouds pods are SNATed at node level; some CNI configs (Calico IPPools with NatOutgoing=false) will preserve pod IP and break egress passthrough.

acme-devops: We're on on-prem with Calico. Our IPPool had natOutgoing: false for policy reasons. We rely on a central gateway 3.21.45.33 for outbound and firewall only allows that source.

sarah: That explains it. Two immediate remediations:
1) Allow DNS from the pod to kube-dns (UDP 53 to 10.96.0.10) in NetworkPolicy.
2) Either enable SNAT for pod egress (set natOutgoing: true on the IPPool or ensure node iptables MASQUERADE) or add egress rules to permit the pod CIDR on the firewall (less recommended).

Suggested temporary NP to unblock (apply to redwood-private):
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: redwood-egress-temporary-allow
  namespace: redwood-private
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redwood-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.96.0.10/32    # kube-dns
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 53
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 54.210.99.0/24  # control-plane (example)
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

mike: If your infra requires SNAT, enabling natOutgoing on Calico IPPool is the right long-term change. If you re-enable SNAT please test other services that depend on original pod IPs.

acme-devops: We applied the temporary NP and toggled natOutgoing=true on the calico ippool. Restarted agent.

acme-devops logs after change:
```
[2026-04-02T14:25:07Z] INFO starting redwood-agent v2.2.0
[2026-04-02T14:25:08Z] INFO resolved control.redwood.example.com -> 54.210.99.12
[2026-04-02T14:25:08Z] INFO connecting to control-plane via 54.210.99.12:443
[2026-04-02T14:25:09Z] INFO TLS handshake complete, cert CN=control.redwood.example.com
[2026-04-02T14:25:09Z] INFO registration succeeded, agent id: ag-7788
```

acme-devops: Agent registered in console. Thanks!

dan: Additional notes for your gitops repo: commit a NetworkPolicy that explicitly allows DNS and control-plane CIDRs for agent pods, and document Calico natOutgoing expectations. Also add an e2e CI check that runs a simple `curl` from the agent pod after NP changes.

sarah: One more edge-case: if you're behind an HTTP/TLS intercepting proxy (corporate), the agent may connect through an HTTP CONNECT and you could get x509 UnknownAuthorityError. If that happens you must either trust the proxy CA in the agent/container or allow direct egress to Redwood control-plane. Not needed here but worth logging in runbook.

acme-devops: We'll update docs and tests. Closing. :white_check_mark:

netbot: Created support ticket SPT-2026-1120 and linked to INC-2026-1120
deploy-bot: Incident INC-2026-1120 resolved (agent registration restored)
